claims.text: The starting FeNiCrCoCu nanoparticles are initially solid, homogeneous, crystalline, and single phase.
Heating FeNiCrCoCu nanoparticles in the premelting regime produces a disordered, compositionally segregated surface layer.
The segregated surface layer initiates melting below the temperature expected from bulk and particle-size effects alone.
Surface passivation inhibits surface diffusion in the nanoparticles.
Elevated temperature accelerates surface diffusion of the constituent alloy elements.
Differential elemental diffusion causes local compositional fluctuations and interfacial disorder.
A compositionally segregated and disordered surface layer destabilizes the crystalline lattice.
Surface-layer-induced lattice destabilization reduces the energy barrier for melting of the nanoparticle core.
A disordered surface region and elemental segregation will appear before complete nanoparticle melting.
Nanoparticles exhibiting surface segregation will begin melting at a lower effective temperature than the homogeneous baseline or passivated comparison.
The extent and temperature of the proposed premelting behavior may vary with nanoparticle size and heating rate.
Rapid bulk-melting kinetics can overwhelm the surface-diffusion-controlled process.
